snapshot-revert-snapshot-before: Take a snapshot of the VM before reverting
snapshot-revert-warning: This will restore the VM to the selected snapshot state. Any changes made since then (data, configuration, and disk state) will be lost. This action cannot be undone.
snapshots-found-description: {disks} have a snapshot from {date} on {sr}. If they are restored to this storage, a differential restore will be attempted: only the blocks that differ are transferred. Otherwise, or if it fails, they are fully copied.
source-backup-repository-by-default-info: The source repository by default. Other repositories served by {proxy} are listed too.

sr-preferred-image-formats-info: Disk formats in descending order of priority.
sr-preferred-image-formats-qcow2-warning: Qcow2 support must be installed on the host.
sr-usage-exceeds-80-percent: Storage usage has exceeded 80% of total capacity. Performance may be impacted, consider freeing up space.
sr-usage-exceeds-90-percent: Storage usage has exceeded 90% of total capacity. Free up space immediately to avoid service disruption.

start-host: Start the host to resume operations, or check back later once it’s powered on.

store-replicas-on-every-storage-reposito: Store replicas on every selected remote storage repository
stores-what-vm-writes-reachable-by-proxy: Stores what {vm} writes. Must be reachable by {proxy}.

template-has-bios-strings: The template already contains the BIOS strings
the-disk-depends-on-proxy: The disk depends on {proxy}: it is detached if the proxy stops, restarts or is updated.
the-disk-is-served-read-only-from-the-ba: The disk is served read-only from the backup. Nothing is copied.
the-file-goes-into-the-xo-exports-folder: The file goes into the xo-exports folder, at the root of the repository. The folder is created if needed.
the-file-takes-the-full-size-of-the-disk: the file takes the full size of the disk
the-host-where-the-chosen-vm-runs: The host where the chosen VM runs

theme-monokai-description: Colorful theme inspired by code editors

traffic-rules:edit-order-info: Traffic rules are evaluated by priority, starting with rule 1, then rule 2, and so on. The first matching rule is applied, and subsequent rules are skipped. Priority only matters within the same network.
traffic-rules:edit-order-save-info: Changes will only take effect when you save.
traffic-rules:error-plugin: You are using the direct OpenFlow protocol (legacy mode), which does not support network traffic rules. To create them, switch to the XAPI plugin mode (beta) — see {check-doc}.
traffic-rules:format-warning: Configuration error: Traffic rules are not in the expected format. Please {check-doc} on how to migrate them.
traffic-rules:no-free-priority: No priority left below the other rules of {network}

unable-to-connect-to-xo-server: Unable to connect to XO server.

untranslated-text-helper: By default, untranslated texts will be presented in english.
v2v:check:n-snapshots: 1 snapshot on the source VM | {n} snapshots on the source VM
v2v:check:no-snapshot: No snapshot on the source VM
v2v:credentials-never-stored: Credentials are never stored by XO: they stay in this browser and are sent with each request that needs VMware. Migration status is shared by everyone who connects to the same vCenter.
v2v:default-options-info: Apply to every VM unless overridden below
v2v:destination-pool-info: A migration goes from one source to one pool. Each source and pool pair has its own list.
v2v:docking-vm-info: Once the import is complete, the VM boots on the docking ISO of the pool, which installs the Xen drivers and the guest agent and disables the VMware tools. Needs a complete import and a docking ISO on the pool.
v2v:existing-list-info: This browser already holds a migration list for {migration} ({vms}). Continuing reopens it, with the current migration state of every VM.
v2v:filter-vms-info: Filter by datastore, status or name with the query builder
v2v:global-defaults-info: Applied to every VM, disk and network adapter. Each VM can override them in step 4 (Mapping). The SR and network are prefilled with the pool default SR and the management network of the pool master.
v2v:launch-success: The migration is running: its task tells its progress.
v2v:list-pair-info: One source and one destination per list: choosing another source or pool opens its own list.
v2v:migrated-vm-details: Existing VM: {vm} on pool {pool}, SR {srs}. A second VM will be created on pool {destinationPool}.
v2v:migration-list-of-newer-version: A newer version of Xen Orchestra stored this migration list. Reload the page to continue with it.
v2v:next-run-reminder: The longer since the last sync, the larger the final delta. Run a delta sync shortly before the cutover to keep the downtime short.
v2v:no-vm-in-list: No VM in the migration list
v2v:prerequisite-error: Prerequisite check: vectura cannot be used, VMs cannot be migrated until it is fixed
v2v:prerequisite-error-detail: Prerequisite check: vectura cannot be used ({error}), VMs cannot be migrated until it is fixed
v2v:remove-from-list-info: Only the migration list changes: nothing is deleted on the source nor in XO.
v2v:source-snapshot-changed-info: If the source snapshot changed since the last sync, a new VM is created with the global defaults and the partial import is left as is.
v2v:start-blocked-partial: Start blocked while the import is partial
v2v:start-vm-on-xcp-ng-info: VM started once its import is complete. The first boot of a docked guest is followed. Needs a complete import.
v2v:stop-on-error-info: Stop on the first error when importing VMs. Applies to the whole launch.
v2v:stop-source-vm-info: Source VM stopped before the last delta transfer (after final snapshot). Needed to fully transfer a running VM.
v2v:tags-backup-info: Use tags to pick up the VM in smart backup jobs.
v2v:tags-mac-not-applied: Tags and the Keep MAC addresses option of the mapping step are not applied yet.
vdi-allocated-space-exceeds-sr: Allocated space exceeds available capacity on this SR. Proceed with caution.

vdi-delete-warning: This will permanently delete the selected VDI and all data stored on it. This action cannot be undone.
vdi-detach-info: This will detach the selected VDI from the VM. The disk will not be deleted and can be reattached later.
vdi-detach-title: You are about to detach 1 VDI | You are about to detach {n} VDIs
vdi-disconnect-info: The VM will no longer have access to the VDI. The disk remains attached and you can reconnect later.
vdi-disconnect-title: You are about to disconnect 1 VDI | You are about to disconnect {n} VDIs
vdi-on-different-sr-warning: This SR is local to a host that doesn't hold the VM's other disks. The VM won't be able to start until all its disks are on the same host or on shared storage.
vif-connect-title: You are about to connect 1 VIF | You are about to connect {n} VIFs

vif-disconnect-title: You are about to disconnect 1 VIF | You are about to disconnect {n} VIFs
vm-backup-failure-number-of-retries: Number of retries if VM backup fails
vm-cannot-be-migrated-off-host: {vm} can't be migrated off {host} while the disk is attached.
vm-delete-warning: This will permanently delete the VM, its snapshots and its disks. Disks attached to another VM are kept. This action cannot be undone.
vm-depends-on-proxy: {vm} depends on {proxy}: if the proxy stops, restarts or is updated, {vm} loses its disks and what was written to them.
vm-disable-blocked-protection: To proceed, you can disable the protection in the VM’s configuration.
vm-disable-delete-protection: To remove it, please edit its configuration and disable the deletion protection.
vm-disable-migration-protection: To proceed, please edit its configuration and disable the migration protection.
vm-needs-proxy-while-using-disks: {vm} needs {proxy} for as long as it uses {disks}, which stays in the backup.
vm-not-running-intra-pool-nothing-to-mig: The VM is not running: within its pool, there is no active RAM to migrate. As long as no disk moves to another SR, there is nothing to migrate.
vm-not-running-no-disk-nothing-to-migrat: Nothing to migrate: the VM is not running and has no disk.
vm-off: This virtual machine is powered off.
vm-protected-deletion: This VM is currently protected against deletion.
vm-protected-force-reboot: This VM is protected against force reboot.
vm-protected-force-shutdown: This VM is protected against force shutdown.
vm-protected-migration: This VM is protected against migration.
vm-protected-pause: This VM is protected against pause.
vm-protected-reboot: This VM is protected against reboot.
vm-protected-shutdown: This VM is protected against shutdown.
vm-protected-suspend: This VM is protected against suspend.
warning:vdi-already-attached: The selected VDI is already attached to this VM.
warning:vdi-sr: This SR is not compatible with other VDIs' SRs. The SR needs to be shared or on the same host as the other VDIs' SRs.
what-does-protected-mean-content: A VM is considered protected when it’s included in at least one scheduled backup job and the last three runs of that job completed successfully. This helps ensure the VM has recent, reliable recovery points.
what-is-a-disabled-host-content: A disabled host is a running host on which no new VM can be started. VMs already running on it keep running.
what-is-an-eol-host-content: An EOL (End of Life) host is a server running a version of Xen or an operating system that is no longer supported by its vendor. It no longer receives updates, bug fixes or security patches, which can make it unstable or vulnerable. We recommend upgrading to a supported version to ensure performance, compatibility and security.
what-is-an-unreachable-pool-content: A pool is considered unreachable when Xen Orchestra can no longer communicate with it. This may happen if the pool is offline, the network is misconfigured, or credentials have changed.
what-is-an-unreachable-pool-tip: To restore access, verify the pool is running, check your connection, and ensure credentials are up to date.
zip-description: Opens as is on Windows and macOS.
